task: Make the MCP server test (POST /assistants/mcp/test) resolve inline settings.credential_values when settings.id is absent, limited to the catalog entry's required_env_vars and never logged or persisted, and confirm mcp_tools shares the resolution (EPMCDME-11766).

key_reasoning.reason: Credential handling is security-sensitive. The closest pattern, MCPToolkitService._apply_tool_config_to_mcp_server (tool_creds merged into server_config.env), has no allow-list, so the required_env_vars guard has no precedent (security-gap auto-bump). The acceptance criteria list specific guard cases (only catalog env names, never logged, never persisted), and no existing test template covers that defensive pattern (second auto-bump). _resolve_credentials_with_priority is shared with runtime, workflows and validation, so changing it risks regressions outside the test path. Also settings.id=None currently falls through the handler chain and may match an unrelated stored setting. Scored L rather than XL because there is no performance concern, rollback is trivial, and the helper that converts credential_values to a dict already exists.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk raised from M to L: security and credential-handling requirement (never log or persist values, allow-list of env names) with no existing allow-list precedent
Technical Risk: edge and variant cases in the acceptance criteria with no matching defensive test template (auto-bump, folded into the same L)
